subject: Aligning Order Form caps with Security Addendum for FinTechCo
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Roman <anna@fintechco.com>, Jordan Price <jordan.procurement@fintechco.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Aligning Order Form caps with Security Addendum for FinTechCo

Hi Anna / Jordan —

Thanks again for the productive call yesterday. As requested, I attached an updated Order Form (RW_OrderForm_v3_redlines.docx) that takes the latest MSA edits into account. High-level proposal to resolve the remaining redline tension on liability/caps:

- MSA remains the governing document for overall liability cap (MSA Section 7) — standard 12-month fee cap.
- For security-related incidents only, we propose the Security Addendum to define a dedicated per-incident sub-limit (tied to 12x monthly committed spend) plus mandatory mitigation obligations and notification timelines.
- Carve-outs: intentional misconduct, gross negligence and indemnities for third-party IP claims remain outside the cap as discussed.

Why this approach: it keeps the predictable economic ceiling in the MSA while giving FinTechCo stronger, incident-specific assurances in the Security Addendum that are measurable and limited in scope. This should address procurement concerns about exposure for security events while preserving Redwood's unit economics.

Please see the redlines in the attached Security_Addendum_v2_redlines.pdf; the redline comments call out the exact per-incident number and the proposed waterfall for multiple related incidents. Happy to walk through this on a quick call.

Next steps: if you can share the specific figure FinTechCo would need for per-incident exposure (or a calculation method), we can run it by legal and ops today.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198

Attachments: RW_OrderForm_v3_redlines.docx (docx), Security_Addendum_v2_redlines.pdf (pdf)
From: Anna Roman <anna@fintechco.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Price <jordan.procurement@fintechco.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Aligning Order Form caps with Security Addendum for FinTechCo

Sean —

Appreciate the clear draft. A couple of immediate reactions from FinTechCo Legal:

1) Per-incident cap: Procurement is reluctant to accept a calculation tied to monthly committed spend without an explicit floor. Can you confirm Redwood would accept an absolute per-incident cap (e.g., $2.5M) or a formula capped at a maximum (12x monthly up to $5M)?

2) Waterfall for related incidents: we need language that prevents aggregation across unrelated incidents but allows aggregation for a single root cause. FinTechCo will propose a 90-day grouping window; please flag if that causes operational issues.

3) Carve-outs: we agree on intentional misconduct and IP exclusions, but FinTechCo requests that SOC2 failures that cause material customer impact be excluded from the overall cap (we prefer they fall under the security addendum and have a standalone remedy).

I've attached our spreadsheet (FinTechCo_SecReq_20270602.xlsx) with their risk tolerance numbers. Share with your legal ops and let's set a time tomorrow to resolve the numeric approach.

Thanks —
Anna Roman
External Counsel, FinTechCo
anna@fintechco.com | +1 212-555-0147

Attachment: FinTechCo_SecReq_20270602.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Aligning Order Form caps with Security Addendum for FinTechCo

Sean / Laura —

Couple of operational notes from Security & CS:

- 90-day grouping window is operationally reasonable, but we need to define "related incident" in the Addendum (e.g., same root cause, overlapping affected tenant set, and contiguous incident timeline).
- Evidence and postmortem: FinTechCo wants to preserve audit rights — we can provide third-party attestation reports and a redacted incident timeline but cannot share raw customer logs. Recommend adding a narrow audit scope and a process for redaction.
- Notification timing: 24-hour initial notification + 7-day status cadence for material incidents is our baseline. If FinTechCo requires 12-hour notification, we can accept it only with reciprocal SLA credits tied to response times.

If Legal wants numeric guidance, our ops model says 12x committed monthly spend up to $4M keeps the economics intact for sustained production workloads. Below that, exceptions for repeat incidents should be limited to prevent open-ended exposure.

-Monica
Monica Patel
Director, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Roman <anna@fintechco.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Jordan Price <jordan.procurement@fintechco.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Aligning Order Form caps with Security Addendum for FinTechCo

Anna —

Thanks for the spreadsheet and the clear asks. Thinking through the options, Redwood proposes the following compromise to present to your Procurement team tomorrow:

- Order Form will reference the MSA cap (12-month fees) as the default global cap.
- Security Addendum will contain a standalone per-incident security sub-limit equal to 12x committed monthly spend, with an explicit absolute ceiling of $4,000,000 (i.e., the formula applies up to $4M).
- Related-incidents: we'll adopt FinTechCo's 90-day grouping for aggregation, with the Addendum defining "related incident" as Monica suggested.
- Audit & evidence: Redwood will provide third-party SOC2 reports, a redacted timeline, and a mutually agreed audit scope (no raw tenant logs).
- Notification windows: Redwood accepts 24-hour initial notification and 7-day cadence. If FinTechCo needs 12-hour initial notice, Redwood requests SLA credits for materially increased ops overhead; propose we table that until after we agree on the cap numbers.

If that sounds workable, I can ask Legal to put these bullet points into the Security_Addendum_v3 and share a single tracked-redline set for execution.

Quick ask: can you confirm the maximum per-incident ceiling FinTechCo would be comfortable with (is $4M acceptable)? If so, we aim to get a doc for signature next week.

Best,
Sean
From: Anna Roman <anna@fintechco.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Price <jordan.procurement@fintechco.com>, FinTechCo Legal <legal@fintechco.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Aligning Order Form caps with Security Addendum for FinTechCo

Sean / team —

This is helpful and closer to what Procurement needs. A few final items from Legal before we mark green:

- FinTechCo can live with a 12x committed monthly spend up to $4M as the security sub-limit, provided we get: (a) explicit carve-out language that SOC2 failures resulting in customer data exposure are treated as security incidents for the Addendum (and not funneled back under the MSA cap), and (b) a clear indemnity backstop for claims made by affected third parties.
- Please add a clause obligating Redwood to preserve relevant logs for 90 days post-incident for purposes of independent review (with a characterized redaction process).
- We will circulate redlines for the exact indemnity and preservation language; if Redwood's Legal can accept those redlines in principle, we can move to DocuSign.

I'll coordinate with Procurement on the $4M ceiling and confirm tomorrow. Thanks for moving quickly.

—Anna
